evidence.detail: all remove_pd patterns require either a space/boundary or a hyphen around 'penny'; 'Penny31LakeTrickery' has 'penny' immediately followed by a digit with no separator, so no pattern matches
remove_season uses \b word boundaries; in 'Penny31LakeTrickery' after removing 'penny', '31' is surrounded by word chars ('y31L'), so \b does not fire
bakert's comment cites a specific unhandled test case ('Penny31BlueSteel','Penny31bluesteel') and the issue body itself suggests the regex approach is fundamentally limited here

triage.notes: Fix requires either: (a) a new remove_pd sub-pattern that strips 'penny' when immediately followed by digits (e.g. r'^penny(\d+)'), plus a matching remove_season change to strip leading digit+letter sequences, or (b) a more parser-like approach as suggested in the issue body. Both carry non-trivial false-positive risk and need many new test cases.
